## Summary

I reviewed all 10 source files in this tenant-boundary service (no `package.json`, lockfile, config, or env files were present, so there is no dependency-version metadata to audit). I traced data flows from the `authenticate` middleware through every mounted route, considered each taxonomy category, and self-verified to drop non-exploitable items.

**Findings (2 exploitable):**

| Severity | ID | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 CRITICAL | `broken-object-level-authorization` | `GET /api/invoices/:id` fetches by ID only — `req.user.tenantId` is never checked, so any authenticated user reads other tenants' invoices. The tenant-scoped `listForTenant` exists but no route uses it. |
| 🟠 HIGH | `mass-assignment` | `PATCH /api/profile` forwards `req.body` straight into the user update with no allowlist, so `{"role":"admin"}` escalates the caller to admin (the `role` field gates `/api/admin`). |

**Considered and ruled out as non-exploitable:** SQL injection (all queries use `$1` parameterization), path traversal (`avatarPath` has a correct `ROOT + sep` guard and its router isn't even mounted — a decoy), XSS (only `res.json` output), authentication bypass (HS256 pinned, env secret; `verifyJwt` is a stub that 500s rather than bypasses), hardcoded secrets, CORS/redirect/SSRF/SSTI/command-injection/deserialization/proto-pollution (no matching sinks), and vulnerable-dependency (no dependency metadata present).

`source_modified` is `false`.
